annotation_description: Playing Flooded Strand (which can only fetch Plains or Island) means the player cannot produce black mana this turn to cast Fatal Push on Ocelot Pride. This gives the opponent a free attack with Ocelot Pride (gaining life via lifelink) and a token at end step, letting the board spiral out of control.

Fetched Godless Shrine and paid 2 life to enter untapped for black mana, but they had a Swamp already in hand that could provide black mana for Thoughtseize this turn. The 2 life paid for the shockland was unnecessary.

With Ocelot Pride on the board (a 1/1 creature), Fatal Push would cleanly destroy it for just 1 mana, and the opponent already has revolt enabled (no permanents left the battlefield, but Fatal Push doesn't need revolt for a 1-mana creature). Casting Thoughtseize costs 2 life (putting Valley at 15) and only takes a card from hand, while the Ocelot Pride on the battlefield continues to threaten token generation at end of turn. Fatal Push removes the immediate board threat efficiently. Thoughtseize is better when you need information or to strip a key card before the opponent can cast it, but the Ocelot Pride is already deployed and will generate value if it survives to the end step. That said, Thoughtseize does provide information and can strip a follow-up threat, and Valley still has Orcish Bowmasters available to flash in during the end step to potentially deal with token generation, so this is close but slightly suboptimal.

Fetched a second Godless Shrine and paid 2 life (going from 13 to 11) when a basic Swamp would have entered untapped for free and provided the same mana to cast Orcish Bowmasters. Against an aggressive Ocelot Pride deck, 2 life is meaningful.

Played Orcish Bowmasters to ping the Cat Token instead of using Fatal Push to kill Ocelot Pride, the primary snowball threat. Ocelot Pride left alive can continue generating tokens whenever another creature deals combat damage. Bowmasters' flash ability is wasted by playing it on your own main phase rather than holding it for the opponent's draw step or as an instant-speed response.

The Orcish Bowmasters ETB trigger deals 1 damage to any target and amasses Orcs 1. Targeting the Cat Token (1/1) kills it, which is fine, but targeting Ocelot Pride (1/1) would be significantly more impactful. Ocelot Pride is the engine that creates Cat tokens every end step when life is gained - it's the key threat that will snowball if left unchecked. The Cat Token is just a vanilla 1/1, while Ocelot Pride generates ongoing value. Killing Ocelot Pride with the 1 damage ping would remove the token-generating engine entirely.

Cast Galvanic Discharge before playing Sacred Foundry, likely using Arena of Glory's mana. This prevented the line of playing Sacred Foundry first, using it to pay for Galvanic Discharge, then exerting Arena of Glory for RR + Plains for 1 to cast Seasoned Pyromancer with haste. The hasty Pyromancer would apply significant pressure against the 11-life opponent while generating card filtering and tokens.

Attacking a 1/1 Orc Army Token into an opponent with Ocelot Pride (1/1 first strike, lifelink) on the battlefield. If the opponent blocks, they kill the token without losing Ocelot Pride (first strike), gain 1 life (triggering Ocelot Pride's end-step token creation), and we lose our only creature. If they don't block, we deal 1 but lose a valuable blocker that could prevent Ocelot Pride from attacking and gaining life next turn.

Ocelot Pride is a 1/1 that generates tokens at end step whenever the opponent gains life. With lifelink on the Pride itself, it will create a cat token every turn it deals combat damage. This can snowball quickly. Fatal Push costs only {B} and Ocelot Pride has mana value 1, so it's a clean removal target. The opponent has Sacred Foundry and Arena of Glory tapped, meaning they likely can't protect it. Letting Ocelot Pride survive means it could attack next turn, gain life via lifelink, and create a token at end step, beginning to snowball.

Playing Swamp instead of Flooded Strand is slightly suboptimal. Flooded Strand as a fetch land enables Revolt for Fatal Push, which is highly relevant since the opponent has Ocelot Pride on board (1/1 that will generate tokens). With two Fatal Pushes in hand and the opponent's Ocelot Pride being a critical threat that needs answering, having a fetch land on the battlefield ready to sacrifice for Revolt gives much more flexibility. The Swamp just provides black mana which is already available from two Godless Shrines. Playing the fetch land now keeps open the option to crack it on the opponent's turn to enable Revolt-powered Fatal Push to kill larger threats (up to MV 4) if needed, while still providing mana access.

Casting Seasoned Pyromancer before playing Mountain forces exerting Arena of Glory to generate {R}{R}, meaning Arena won't untap next turn. Playing Mountain first provides the third red source, allowing Seasoned Pyromancer to be cast with Mountain + Sacred Foundry + Plains without needing to exert Arena of Glory.

Cast a second Fatal Push targeting Ocelot Pride when there was already a Fatal Push on the stack targeting the same creature. The first Fatal Push alone would destroy the 1-mana Ocelot Pride, making the second copy completely wasted. This throws away a premium removal spell for no benefit.

Playing Plains instead of Flooded Strand is slightly suboptimal. Flooded Strand provides deck thinning and, more importantly, can enable Revolt for Fatal Push (relevant if drawn later or in future turns). Additionally, fetching with Flooded Strand puts a land in the graveyard, which helps fuel Phlage's escape cost if the player ever needs to use graveyard resources. The player already has cards in the graveyard including Fatal Push copies, so having a fetch land available on the battlefield to crack at instant speed for Revolt is more valuable than saving 1 life. With the opponent at 20 and the player at 11, the 1 life matters somewhat, but the tactical flexibility of a fetch land on board outweighs this.

Casting Emperor of Bones in the precombat main phase when the opponent has 3 open mana (Plains, Arena of Glory, Sacred Foundry) that could represent removal or interaction. The opponent's graveyard contains Galvanic Discharge, and they play a Boros deck that likely has removal. Additionally, Emperor of Bones's combat trigger won't exile anything useful from the opponent's graveyard this turn since it triggers at the beginning of combat - though it could target Phlage to prevent escape, which is actually valuable. However, playing a 2/2 into an opponent who could have Thraben Charm or other removal with no immediate value (the adapt costs additional mana) is somewhat risky. The alternative of holding up Flooded Strand + passing to represent interaction or waiting could be considered, though Emperor of Bones exiling Phlage from the opponent's graveyard at beginning of combat is genuinely important to prevent the escape threat.

Emperor of Bones likely has a creature exiled with it from the beginning of combat trigger (probably Orcish Bowmasters from own graveyard). With 1B available from untapped Godless Shrine and Plains, adapting Emperor of Bones in response to Thraben Charm would make it a 4/4 and reanimate the exiled creature with haste. This is significant value being left on the table.

Emperor of Bones likely exiled Phlage from the opponent's graveyard at the beginning of combat. Activating Adapt 2 for {1}{B} would put +1/+1 counters on Emperor, triggering its ability to reanimate Phlage with haste. Phlage's ETB deals 3 damage and gains 3 life, and it would attack as a 6/6 this turn. The player had the mana available (Godless Shrine + Plains untapped). Even if Phlage wasn't exiled, other creatures like Ocelot Pride or Orcish Bowmasters could have been exiled and reanimated.

Emperor of Bones has an Adapt 2 ability for {1}{B}, and the player has 2 untapped lands (Godless Shrine and Plains) available to pay for it. Adapting would put +1/+1 counters on Emperor of Bones, making it a 4/4, and trigger its ability to put a creature card exiled with it onto the battlefield with haste. Even if no creature is currently exiled with it (the beginning of combat trigger may have exiled something), making Emperor a 4/4 is pure upside with no downside. The player has mana available and nothing else to spend it on, so declining to use this mana sink wastes resources.

Gem25F Valley has Flooded Strand in hand and should play it as their land drop during precombat main phase. Missing land drops when you have lands available is always suboptimal, especially when it could provide additional mana for adapt activation or future plays. The reasoning also incorrectly states it's MiMo Sarge's turn when it's actually Gem25F Valley's turn 5.

Emperor of Bones could have been adapted for {1}{B} during combat using the two untapped lands (Godless Shrine + Plains). This would make it a 4/4 attacker and potentially reanimate a creature exiled with its beginning-of-combat trigger (likely Ocelot Pride from opponent's graveyard), giving it haste for additional combat damage.

annotation_description: Emperor of Bones likely exiled a creature from a graveyard at the beginning of combat this turn. Activating Adapt 2 for {1}{B} during combat would make Emperor of Bones a 4/4 AND trigger its ability to put the exiled creature onto the battlefield with haste, giving an additional attacker. The player had plenty of mana available (4 lands untapped) and declined this significant combat advantage.

Emperor of Bones is a high-value engine piece that can reanimate creatures from graveyards (Phlage, Ocelot Pride, Orcish Bowmasters are all valid targets). Attacking it into a Seasoned Pyromancer that can profitably trade risks losing this engine for just 2 damage against 20 life. The opponent has incentive to block since Seasoned Pyromancer already got its ETB value.

Emperor of Bones (2/2) was attacking into Seasoned Pyromancer (2/2) and they traded. Adapting Emperor of Bones for {1}{B} would have made it a 4/4, letting it survive combat, kill Seasoned Pyromancer, and potentially trigger the +1/+1 counter ability to reanimate an exiled creature with haste. The mana was available (untapped Godless Shrines, Swamp, Plains).

MiMo Sarge could have escaped Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury this turn using Mountain (R to pay Arena's exert cost), Arena of Glory exerted (RR), Sacred Foundry (W), Plains (W) for exactly RRWW, exiling 5 of the 8 graveyard cards. This would put a 6/6 on the board, deal 3 damage to the opponent (putting them to 7), and gain 3 life. Instead they played Sacred Foundry and passed up deploying the most impactful threat available against an opponent at 10 life with an empty board.

MiMo Sarge has exactly enough mana (RRWW from 5 lands) and enough cards in graveyard (7 other cards, need 5) to escape Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury. The opponent is at 10 life with no creatures on board. Phlage would enter as a 6/6, deal 3 damage (opponent to 7), gain 3 life, and threaten another 3 damage on attack next turn. This is a game-dominating play that was completely passed on.

Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury can be escaped here for {R}{R}{W}{W} exiling 5 cards from the 7 available in graveyard. It creates a 6/6 body, deals 3 damage to the opponent (putting them to 7), and gains 3 life. This is vastly superior to Seasoned Pyromancer's graveyard ability which only creates two 1/1 tokens. Phlage threatens lethal next attack (6 combat + 3 trigger = 9 vs opponent's 10, nearly lethal) and applies enormous pressure.

With the opponent at 7 life, Phlage escape was available (RRWW + exile 5 cards from 8-card graveyard) for a 6/6 that deals 3 damage on entry (putting opponent to 4) and gains 3 life. Playing Elegant Parlor (tapped land) as the first action is suboptimal sequencing - if they plan to cast Phlage this turn, they should lead with Phlage to avoid revealing information. If they don't cast Phlage at all, it's a much bigger mistake. Additionally, Arid Mesa would have been a better land drop as it can fetch an untapped land.

At 7 life, played Watery Grave paying 2 life (going to 5) before casting Thoughtseize. They already have B mana available from Swamp/Godless Shrine to cast Thoughtseize this turn. Should cast Thoughtseize first to see opponent's hand and gather information before committing to a land drop. Additionally, paying 2 life for Watery Grave to enter untapped is likely unnecessary since they already have 6 lands with all colors available - it could safely enter tapped.

At 5 life with Phlage in opponent's graveyard (which deals exactly 3 on ETB), paying 2 life for Thoughtseize drops to 3 life - exactly in Phlage escape lethal range. The opponent has enough mana colors (2x Sacred Foundry, Mountain, Arena of Glory, Plains) and 9 cards in graveyard (needs 5 to exile) to potentially escape Phlage next turn for exactly lethal.

Casting Thoughtseize at 5 life drops Gem25F Valley to 3 life, which puts them in lethal range of Phlage's escape (3 damage ETB trigger). The opponent has Phlage in graveyard with 9 cards available to exile 5, and enough mana ({R}{R}{W}{W}) across their lands. At 5 life, Phlage's 3 damage is survivable; at 3 life it's lethal. The only nonland card taken (Voice of Victory, a 1/3) is not worth the risk.

Opponent is at 3 life and Phlage, Titan of Fire's Fury can be escaped from the graveyard for {R}{R}{W}{W} + exile 5 cards. MiMo Sarge has 9 cards in graveyard (enough to exile 5) and the mana to pay {R}{R}{W}{W} (Mountain, Arena of Glory for {R}{R}, Plains and Sacred Foundry/Elegant Parlor for {W}{W}). Phlage's ETB deals 3 damage to any target, which is exactly lethal against the opponent at 3 life.

Opponent is at 3 life. MiMo Sarge has Phlage in the graveyard with escape cost {R}{R}{W}{W} + exile 5 cards (9 other cards available in graveyard). With Sacred Foundry entering untapped (pay 2 life), the 4 untapped lands (Arena of Glory, existing Sacred Foundry, existing Elegant Parlor, new Sacred Foundry) would produce exactly {R}{R}{W}{W} to escape Phlage. Phlage's ETB deals 3 damage to any target, which is exactly lethal against the opponent at 3 life. Instead, Elegant Parlor enters tapped, leaving only 3 untapped lands and making Phlage uncastable this turn.

At 3 life facing lethal on board (Voice of Victory + Ragavan = 5+ damage next attack), spending 1 life to fetch a land with 8 lands already in play is wasteful. Voice of Victory is MV 2, so Fatal Push already kills it without needing revolt. The life point matters significantly at 3 life.

Gem25F Valley is at 3 life facing lethal next turn from Ragavan (2/1) + Voice of Victory (1/3 with Mobilize 2 creating two 1/1 attackers) = 5 damage. Voice of Victory also prevents casting spells during opponent's turn, so they can't Fatal Push during MiMo's combat. They have the mana to hard-cast Solitude (3WW with 7+ untapped lands) to exile Voice of Victory, which would remove the spell-lock, the mobilize tokens, and leave Solitude as a 3/2 lifelink blocker against Ragavan.

Voice of Victory prevents opponents from casting spells during MiMo Sarge's turn. At 3 life, Gem25F Valley faces lethal from Ragavan (2/1) + Voice of Victory (1/3) + two Mobilize warrior tokens. By passing without removing Voice of Victory or Ragavan, Gem25F Valley will be completely locked out of casting Solitude or Fatal Push during MiMo Sarge's next combat, making lethal unavoidable.

Opponent is at 3 life and MiMo Sarge has no cards in hand except a land. Activating Seasoned Pyromancer from the graveyard for {3}{R}{R} would create two 1/1 Elemental tokens, providing additional attackers to close out the game next turn against an opponent at 3 life. With 6 untapped lands and nothing else to spend mana on, there's no reason not to activate this.
